'''Anthony Joseph Arduengo III''' is Professor of the Practice at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], Saxon Professor Emeritus of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Alabama]], adjunct professor at the Institute for Inorganic Chemistry of [[Braunschweig University of Technology]] in Germany, and co-founder of the ''StanCE'' coalition for sustainable chemistry based on woody biomass ([https://xylochemistry.com/portal/ Xylochemistry]). He is notable for his work on chemical compounds with unusual [[valence (chemistry)|valency]], especially in the field of [[stable carbene]] research.

==Early life==
Anthony "Bo" Arduengo was born in 1952 in [[Tampa, Florida]].<ref name=accchem1>{{cite journal | author = A. J. Arduengo | s2cid = 97034071 | title = Looking for Stable Carbenes: The Difficulty in Starting Anew | year = 1976 | journal = [[Accounts of Chemical Research]] | volume = 32 | issue = 11 | pages = 913–921 | doi = 10.1021/ar980126p}}</ref> He grew up in the [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] area. His father was a pressman and mechanic with the ''[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' and instilled his son with an interest and skill for all things mechanical and scientific. By the age of 16, he and his father had built his first car from miscellaneous parts.<ref>Talon (Walker High School paper), Vol. V, No. 1. September, 1968.</ref> The car was registered as street-legal and road-worthy. With some re-engineering, the car was later fitted to run on alternate fuels including alcohol and hydrogen (which would foretell Arduengo's professional research involvement with [[George W. Bush|President Bush]]'s 2003 National Hydrogen Fuel Initiative (HFI)<ref name=HFI>[http://scienceblog.com/887/white-house-explains-bushs-hydrogen-car-plan/ HFI] - Hydrogen Fuel Initiative. Retrieved 2010-10-04.</ref> and [[United States Department of Energy]]'s Chemical [[Hydrogen Storage]] Program by more than 30 years).

==Education==
Arduengo attended Bouldercrest and Meadowview Elementary Schools, and [[Walker High School (Atlanta, Georgia)|Walker High School]].<ref name="homepage">[http://ajarduengo.net/ Anthony J. Arduengo III] – personal home page. Retrieved 2021-01-02.</ref> In 1969 he left high school with enrollment in Georgia Tech's Joint Enrollment Program for High School Students (JEPHS).<ref name="JEPHS">[http://admission.gatech.edu/dual-enrollment JEPHS] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100905081416/http://www.admission.gatech.edu/jointenrollment/|date=September 5, 2010}} - Georgia Tech's Joint Enrollment Program. Retrieved 2010-10-04.</ref> He obtained his [[bachelor degree|BSc]] (1974, [[cum laude]]) and his [[doctoral degree|PhD]] (1976) at [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]], advised by [[Edward M. Burgess]].<ref name=thesis>
 Anthony Joseph Arduengo (1976), ''The synthesis, structure and chemistry of substituent-perturbed [http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0147Viewer.html thione ''S''-methylides] and [http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0145Viewer.html ''S'',''S''-dihalothiones]'' Ph.D. Thesis, Georgia Institute of Technology. [http://hdl.handle.net/1853/27865 Online catalog entry]. Retrieved 2009-12-04.</ref> That made him an [[academic lineage|academic descendant]] of [[Justus von Liebig]].<ref name=homepage/> As an undergraduate at [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]], Arduengo's research activities began in the laboratory of Professor Charles L. Liotta. He was awarded [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] undergraduate fellowships in 1972 & 1973 when he had moved to research in the [[Edward M. Burgess|Burgess]] group.<ref name=homepage />

As an undergraduate, Arduengo was a member of the [[Georgia Tech Band]] and served as Executive Officer and Captain for that organization. In 1971 he was inducted into the Iota chapter<ref name = Iota>[http://kkpsiiota.gtorg.gatech.edu/index.php Georgia Tech's Iota Chapter of Kappa Kappa Psi]. Retrieved 2017-10-07.</ref> of [[Kappa Kappa Psi]]. In 1972 he was tapped by the Alpha Eta Circle<ref name=AEC>[http://odk.gatech.edu/ Alpha Eta Circle] - Georgia Tech's Alpha Eta Circle of ΟΔΚ. Retrieved 2013-02-08.</ref> of [[Omicron Delta Kappa]]; later serving as Secretary and President for the local Circle.

==Career==
Arduengo was a research scientist at [[DuPont]] from 1976 to 1977, and from 1984 to 1998, and [[assistant professor]] at the [[University of Illinois]] from 1977 to 1984.<ref name=homepage /> He retired from teaching in 2018 and is now Professor of the Practice in the School of Chemistry and Biochemistry at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], Saxon Chair Emeritus of Chemistry at the [[University of Alabama]], and holds a position as adjunct professor at the [[Braunschweig University of Technology|Technische Universität]] in [[Braunschweig]], [[Germany]].<ref name=homepage /><ref name="CV">{{Cite web|url=http://ajarduengo.net/AJA_Web_CV.pdf|title=AJ Arduengo Curriculum Vitae|last=Arduengo|first=Anthony J|date=2021-01-02}}</ref>

In [[DuPont Central Research|DuPont's Central Research and Development Department]], Arduengo began his career in the Chemical Sciences Section (1977 & on return in 1984). In 1988, he was appointed ''Research Leader''. A move into the Polymer Science section of [[DuPont Central Research|CR&D]] in 1991 was accompanied by promotion to ''Group Leader''. His final position with [[DuPont]] was as ''Research Fellow'' which he attained in 1995. The award of an [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander von Humboldt Senior Research Prize]] in 1996 began Arduengo's transition back into academe. The one year Humboldt award was spent in [[Braunschweig]], [[Germany]] at the [[Braunschweig University of Technology|Technical University]]. On return to [[DuPont]], Arduengo maintained a guest Professor appointment in [[Braunschweig]], and in 1999 also made the transition to academe in the U.S. with his assumption of the Saxon Chair in Chemistry at The [[University of Alabama]] in [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama|Tuscaloosa]].<ref name=homepage /><ref name="CV" />

==Research==
===Graduate research at Georgia Tech===
Arduengo's research interests focus largely on the chemistry of new or unusual bonding arrangements, and unusual [[Valence (chemistry)|valency]]. As a graduate student in the [[Edward M. Burgess|Burgess]] group, his research involved organo-[[main group element]] chemistry, specifically, thiocarbonyl [[ylides]], and low-coordinate [[Hypervalent molecules|hypervalent]] [[sulfur]] compounds.<ref name=thesis /><ref>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=E. M. Burgess | title = Syntheses and reactions of substituent stabilized thione methylides | year = 1976 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 98 | issue = 16 | pages = 1520–1521 | doi = 10.1021/ja00432a056|bibcode=1976JAChS..98.5020A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=E. M. Burgess | title = The structure of a substituent stabilized thione methylide | year = 1976 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 98 | issue = 16 | pages = 1521–1523 | doi = 10.1021/ja00432a057|bibcode=1976JAChS..98.5021A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=E. M. Burgess | title = Tricoordinate hypervalent sulfur compounds | year = 1977 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 99 | issue = 2 | pages = 2376–2377 | doi = 10.1021/ja00449a078|bibcode=1977JAChS..99.2376A }}</ref><br />

===DuPont 1977===
In 1977 when he joined [[DuPont (1802-2017)|E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company]], Arduengo became a member of the exploratory chemistry group of [[Howard Ensign Simmons Jr.|Howard Simmons]] in [[DuPont Central Research|CR&D]].<ref name=homepage /> His first research project involved [[trimethylsilyl]] [[ester]]s of [[Mineral acid|inorganic acid]]s as [[reagent]]s for [[organic synthesis]].

=== University of Illinois 1978–1984 ===
At [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|Illinois]] Arduengo examined more broadly the areas of organo-[[main group element]] chemistry, and molecules containing unusual [[Valence (chemistry)|valency]]. His first publications involving the chemistry of [[electron-deficient]] [[carbene]]s occurred during this period.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. P. Janulis |author2=A. J. Arduengo | title = Diazotetrakis(trifluoromethyl)cyclopentadiene and ylides of electronegative elements | url = http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0103Viewer.html | year = 1983 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 105 | issue = 11 | pages = 3563–3567 | doi = 10.1021/ja00349a032|bibcode=1983JAChS.105.3563J | url-access = subscription }}</ref> This work with electron deficient carbenes led to the first structure determinations on a [[nitrile ylide]]<ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. P. Janulis |author2=S. R. Wilson |author3=A. J. Arduengo | title = The synthesis and structure of a stabilized nitrilium ylide | journal = [[Tetrahedron Letters]] | volume = 25 | pages = 405–408| doi = 10.1016/S0040-4039(00)99896-4 | year = 1984 | issue=4}}</ref> and a carbonyl [[ylide]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. P. Janulis |author2=A. J. Arduengo | title = carbonyl ylide | year = 1983 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 105 | issue = 18 | pages = 5929–5930 | doi = 10.1021/ja00356a044 | url=http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0102Viewer.html| url-access = subscription }}</ref> His later work with [[carbene]] chemistry would become his most recognized contribution to the field of chemistry (''vide infra''). During the Illinois years Arduengo had a close collaboration with his colleague [[James Cullen Martin|J.C. Martin]] who was a physical-organic chemist also working on organo-[[main group element]] chemistry and hypervalency. Many of the technical discussions between Martin and Arduengo would take place over lunch (the choice of restaurants often influenced by the quality of the napkins for writing chemical structures).<ref>A.J. Arduengo "''From Hypervalent Compounds to Hypovalent Carbenes''", J.C. Martin Symposium: '''From σ-Constants to σ-Aromaticity''' (Vanderbilt University, May, 1992)</ref> To facilitate discussions about unusual molecular structures and bonding for [[Main group element|main-group element]] centers, Martin and Arduengo devised the [[Hypervalent molecule#N-X-L notation|N-X-L nomenclature system]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=C. W. Perkins |author2=J. C. Martin |author3=A. J. Arduengo |author4=W. Lau |author5=A. Alegria |author6=J. K. Kochi | title = An electrically neutral σ-sulfuranyl radical from the homolysis of a perester with neighboring sulfenyl sulfur: 9-S-3 species | year = 1980 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 102 | issue = 26 | pages = 7753–7759 | doi = 10.1021/ja00546a019|bibcode=1980JAChS.102.7753P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1126/science.221.4610.509 | author = J. C. Martin | title = "Frozen" transition states: pentavalent carbon ''et al.'' | year = 1983 | journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]] | volume = 221 | issue = 4610 | pages = 509–514 | pmid = 17830935 | bibcode = 1983Sci...221..509M | s2cid = 27306583 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=K. Akiba |author2=Y. Yamamoto | title = Chemistry of hypervalent organic compounds. Fundamental aspects of hypervalent organic compounds. Characteristic features of structure and reactivity of hypervalent organic compounds of main group elements. | year = 1988 | journal = Kikan Kagaku Sosetsu | volume = 34 | pages = 9–39 }}</ref> The synthesis and characterization of the first compound with a planar T-shaped, 10-[[electron]] 3-[[coordination compound|coordinate bonding]] arrangement at a [[phosphorus]] atom, '''ADPO''',<ref>{{cite journal |author1=S. A. Culley |author2=A. J. Arduengo | title = Synthesis and structure of the first 10-P-3 species | year = 1984 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 106 | issue = 4 | pages = 1164–1165 | doi = 10.1021/ja00316a084|bibcode=1984JAChS.106.1164C }}</ref> was also accomplished by the Arduengo group at Illinois and paved the way for a range of novel [[Main group element|main-group element]] chemistry (including the discovery of [[edge inversion]]) on his return to [[DuPont]]. The final Illinois research extended the newly discovered '''ADPO''' chemistry to the arsenic analog ('''ADAsO''').<ref>{{cite journal |author1=S. A. Culley |author2=A. J. Arduengo | title = Synthesis and Structure of the First 10-As-3 Species | year = 1985 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 107 | issue = 4 | pages = 1089–1090 | doi = 10.1021/ja00290a072|bibcode=1985JAChS.107.1089C }}</ref><br />

===DuPont 1984–1999===
On returning to [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] in 1984, Arduengo resumed a position in [[DuPont Central Research|CR&D]] and continued the research into the recently discovered '''ADPO''' molecule and related structures. This line of research proved to be extremely fruitful and resulted in a steady string of publications on new and unusual bonding arrangements.<ref name = Dup1>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=C. A. Stewart |author3=F. Davidson |author4=D. A. Dixon |author5=J. Y. Becker |author6=S. A. Culley |author7=M. B. Mizen | title = The synthesis, structure, and chemistry of 10-Pn-3 systems: tricoordinate hypervalent pnictogen compounds | year = 1987 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 109 | issue = 3 | pages = 627–647 | doi = 10.1021/ja00237a001|bibcode=1987JAChS.109..627A }}</ref><ref name=Dup2>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=C. A. Stewart | title = Low coordinate hypervalent phosphorus | year = 1994 | journal = [[Chemical Reviews]] | volume = 94 | issue = 5 | pages = 1215–1237 | doi = 10.1021/cr00029a003 }}</ref> The '''ADPO''' related chemistry provided a basis for the discovery of a new inversion process, [[edge inversion]], which was fully characterized and modelled by the collaborative work of Arduengo and David A. Dixon at [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]].<ref name=Dup3>{{cite journal |author1=D. A. Dixon |author2=A. J. Arduengo |author3=T. Fukunaga | title = A new inversion process at Group VA (Group 15) elements. Edge inversion through a planar T-shaped structure | year = 1986 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 108 | issue = 9 | pages = 2461–2462 | doi = 10.1021/ja00269a063 |pmid=22175610 |bibcode=1986JAChS.108.2461D }}</ref> Additionally, the [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] team provided experimental verification on the new inversion pathway at 3-coordinate [[phosphorus]] centers<ref name=Dup4>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=D. A. Dixon |author3=D. C. Roe | title = Direct determination of the barrier to edge inversion at trivalent phosphorus: verification of the edge inversion mechanism | year = 1986 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 108 | issue = 9 | pages = 6821–6823 | doi = 10.1021/ja00281a070 |bibcode=1986JAChS.108.6821A }}</ref> and a 4-coordinate germanium molecule.<ref name=Dup5>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=D. A. Dixon |author3=D. C. Roe |author4=M. Kline | title = Edge inversion barrier at a four-coordinate main group IV center | year = 1988 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 110 | issue = 13 | pages = 4437–4438 | doi = 10.1021/ja00221a067 |bibcode=1988JAChS.110.4437A }}</ref>

Arduengo's work with [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] also involved a number of applied projects including the flexible [[polyimide]] film, [[Kapton]]-ZT, that is widely used in electronics for flexible printed circuits, connections, and insulation.<ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5272194 | status = patent | title = Process for Preparing a Strengthened Polyimide Film Containing Organometallic Compounds for Improving Adhesion | gdate = 1993-12-21 | fdate = 1992-01-17 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo, Y. C. Ray | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref> Arduengo's research at [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] often coalesced with his other hobbies outside the laboratory; for example with sports cars (''cf.'' photo in the summary box above). He contributed to development of low [[Volatile organic compound|VOC]] automotive coatings by devising [[catalyst]]s for a novel [[cross-link]]ing chemistry used by [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] Performance Coatings in next-generation low-[[Volatile organic compound|VOC]] paints.<ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5034464 | status = patent | title = Amine-Borane Adduct Curing Agents for Epoxy/Anhydride Resins | gdate = 1991-07-23 | fdate = 1989-07-19 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo, | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref><ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5084542 | status = patent | title = Epoxy/Isocyanate Crosslinked Coatings Containing 1,3-Disubstituted Imidazole-2-thione Catalysts | gdate = 1991-01-28 | fdate = 1990-05-31 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo, P. H. Corcoran | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref><ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5091498 | status = patent | title = Curable compositions containing 1,3-dialkylimidazole-2-thione catalysts | gdate = 1993-02-25 | fdate = 1991-02-19 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo, R. J. Barsotti, P. H. Corcoran| assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref> Eventually, [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] waterborne performance coatings would be used by [[Lotus Cars|Lotus]] on their [[Lotus Elise|Elise]] and [[Lotus Exige|Exige]] models.<ref>{{cite journal | author = R. W. Yearich | title = ''Sports Rainbow of Waterborne Finish Paints from DPC'' | year = 2004 | journal = DuPont Refinisher News | volume = Fall | issue = 342 | pages = 4 | url = http://www.britishspeed.com/forum/attachment.php?attachmentid=37588&d=1435605626 | access-date = July 3, 2015}} {{Dead link|date=November 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author = C. A. Sawyer | title = ''Developing the Lotus Elise Series 2'' | year = 2004 | journal = Automotive Design & Production | volume = 6 | url=http://www.autofieldguide.com/articles/developing-the-lotus-elise-series-2 | access-date=June 27, 2015}}</ref> Arduengo's effort on the industrial-scale syntheses<ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5144032 | status = patent | title = Preparation of Tertiary Amine-Borane Adducts | gdate = 1992-09-01 | fdate = 1991-04-19 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref><ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5104993 | status = patent | title = 1,3-Dialkylimidazole-2-thione Catalyst and Method for Making Same | gdate = 1992-04-14 | fdate = 1991-01-31 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref><ref>{{ cite patent | country = US | number = 5182405 | status = patent | title = Preparation of 1,3- Disubstituted Imidazolium Salts | gdate = 1993-01-26 | fdate = 1991-09-18 | inventor = A. J. Arduengo | assign1 = E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Inc.}}</ref> of the [[catalyst]]s for the paints on which he worked would launch his re-entry into the area of [[carbene]] chemistry, but this time it was to be [[nucleophile|nucleophilic]] rather than [[electrophile|electrophilic]] [[carbenes]].<ref name=accchem1 /><ref name=ChiuZ>{{cite journal | author = Anthony J. Arduengo III, Krafczyk Roland | year = 1998 | title = Auf der Suche nach Stabilen Carbenen | journal = Chemie in unserer Zeit | volume = 32 | issue = 1| pages = 6–14 | doi = 10.1002/ciuz.19980320103 }}</ref> The observation that the catalyst syntheses were well tolerant of varied reaction conditions and substituents led Arduengo to postulate that the [[imidazol-2-ylidene]]s that were [[reactive intermediate|intermediates]] in the syntheses had to be far more stable than the then conventional wisdom would allow.<ref name=ChiuZ /><ref name=GT_Cent>A.J. Arduengo "''Cars to Carbenes: A Personal Account of Georgia Tech – Molding Futures One at a Time''," '''Georgia Tech's 100 Years of Chemistry Symposium''' (Atlanta, Georgia, April 19, 2007).</ref>

As Arduengo's involvement in the automotive coatings program came to an end, he submitted a proposal to the management in [[DuPont Central Research|CR&D]] to isolate these apparently [[stable carbene]]s and study their chemistry. The proposal was soundly declined with the admonition that he should have certainly known better than to make such a suggestion in light of the long history of [[carbene]] chemistry that firmly established them as [[reactive intermediate]]s that could not be isolated as stable entities.<ref name=accchem1 /><ref name=ChiuZ /><ref name=GT_Cent /> However, Arduengo (already well-aware of the history) had the starting materials on hand for the chemistry and decided to proceed with the experiments.<ref name=GT_Cent /> "Arduengo's gamble paid off. In 1991, more than 150 years after the first attempt ..."<ref>{{cite journal | author = Cristina Luiggi | title = ''Taming Carbon's Wild Side'' | year = 2009 | journal = Seed Magazine | issue = November 30, 2009 | url=http://seedmagazine.com/content/article/taming_carbons_wild_side/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213045717/http://seedmagazine.com/content/article/taming_carbons_wild_side | url-status=unfit | archive-date=December 13, 2009 | access-date=October 6, 2010}}</ref> a stable crystalline carbene was isolated and characterized in laboratories at [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]].<ref name=carbene1>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=R. L. Harlow |author3=M. Kline | title = A stable crystalline carbene | url = http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0153Viewer.html | year = 1991 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 113 | issue = 1 | pages = 361–363 | doi = 10.1021/ja00001a054|bibcode=1991JAChS.113..361A | url-access = subscription }}</ref> After the first successful reaction to produce a [[persistent carbene|stable carbene]], Arduengo won the support of [[DuPont (1802-2017)|DuPont]] management<ref name=GT_Cent /> and research in this area continued. [[Carbenes]] bearing a variety of substituent groups were prepared and characterized.<ref name=carbene2>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=H. V. R. Dias |author3=R. L. Harlow |author4=M. Kline | title = Electronic stabilization of nucleophilic carbenes | year = 1992 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 114 | issue = 14 | pages = 5530–5534 | doi = 10.1021/ja00040a007 |bibcode=1992JAChS.114.5530A }}</ref><ref name=carbene3>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=R. Krafczyk |author3=R. Schmutzler |author4=H. A. Craig |author5=J. R. Goerlich |author6=W. J. Marshall |author7=M. Unverzagt | title = Imidazolylidenes, imidazolinylidenes and imidazolidines | year = 1992 | journal = [[Tetrahedron (journal)|Tetrahedron]] | volume = 55 | issue = 51 | pages = 14523–14534 | doi = 10.1016/S0040-4020(99)00927-8 }}</ref> The saturated [[Dihydroimidazol-2-ylidene|imidazolin-2-ylidenes]] that were extensively investigated by [[Hans-Werner Wanzlick]] thirty years earlier (without isolation) were now also shown to be stable enough to isolate with appropriate substituents at nitrogen.<ref name=carbene4>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=J. R. Goerlich |author3=W. J. Marshall | title = stable diaminocarbene | year = 1995 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 117 | issue = 44 | pages = 11027–11028 | doi = 10.1021/ja00149a034 |bibcode=1995JAChS.11711027A | url=http://ajarduengo.net/Jmol/htmlfiles/0159Viewer.html| url-access = subscription }}</ref> An air-stable carbene was produced.<ref name=carbene5>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=F. Davidson |author3=H. V. R. Dias |author4=J. R. Goerlich |author5=D. Khasnis |author6=W. J. Marshall |author7=T. K. Prakasha | title = An Air Stable Carbene and Mixed Carbene "Dimers" | year = 1997 | journal = [[J. Am. Chem. Soc.]] | volume = 119 | issue = 52 | pages = 12742–12749 | doi = 10.1021/ja973241o |bibcode=1997JAChS.11912742A }}</ref> The chemistry was extended to include thiazol-2-ylidenes (conjectured to exist in 1957 as a [[reactive intermediate]] in the [[vitamin B1|vitamin B<sub>1</sub>]] [[catalytic cycle]], but not isolated for 40 years).<ref name=carbene6>{{cite journal |author1=A. In 1998, Arduengo and coworkers carefully re-examined the earlier attempts to produce stable carbenes in Wanzlick's laboratory in light of the knowledge and experience gained from the recent successful experiments at DuPont.<ref name=carbene25a>{{cite journal |author1=A. J. Arduengo |author2=J. R. Goerlich |author3=R. Krafczyk |author4=W. J. Marshall | title = 1,3,4,5-Tetraphenylimidazol-2-ylidene: The Realization of Wanzlick's Dream | year = 1998 | journal = [[Angewandte Chemie International Edition]]| volume = 37 | issue = 13–14 | pages = 1963–1965 | doi = 10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19980803)37:13/14<1963::AID-ANIE1963>3.0.CO;2-M }}</ref> Although the majority of Wanzlick's work on the saturated [[Dihydroimidazol-2-ylidene|imidazolin-2-ylidenes]] would have been expected to yield dimers in the absence of bulky substituents on nitrogen, a single (unsaturated) [[imidazol-2-ylidene]], 1,3,4,5-tetraphenylimidazol-2-ylidene, remained as an example of a carbene that could (should) have been isolable. The re-examination of Wanzlick's original procedure<ref name=carbene25b>{{cite journal |author1=H.-J. Schönherr |author2=H.-W. Wanzlick | title = Chemie nucleophiler Carbene, XVIII 1.3.4.5-Tetraphenyl-imidazoliumperchlorat
 | year = 1970 | journal = [[Liebigs Annalen]] | volume = 731 | issue = 1 | pages = 176–179 | doi = 10.1002/jlac.19707310121 }}</ref> identified some key experimental features that would have hindered the original researchers. With these problems corrected, the DuPont scientists were able to isolate the target carbene and fully characterize it including an X-ray structure determination. In a tribute to Hans-Werner Wanzlick, these results were published under the title "1,3,4,5-Tetraphenylimidazol-2-ylidene: The Realization of Wanzlick's Dream."<ref name=carbene25a /><br />

===Georgia Tech 2020–present===
In June 2020 Arduengo returned to his alma mater as Professor of the Practice.<ref name=homepage /><ref name="CV" /><ref name= "ResGate">[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Anthony_Arduengo Anthony J. Arduengo III] – Researchgate. Retrieved 2021-01-02.</ref> His research in carbene chemistry continues there along efforts in support of the Medicines for All Institute<ref name= "M4ALL">[https://medicines4all.vcu.edu/about/m4all-affiliates/ M4ALL] –  affiliates.
